guide_line: Find the limiting reactant, the theoretical yield, and the percent yield.
steps: Divide each mole amount by its coefficient. The smaller result is the limiting reactant. The other reactant is in excess.
Use the limiting reactant and the mole ratio to find moles of product, then grams. That mass is the theoretical yield.
Percent yield = (actual mass / theoretical mass) times 100.

Mass of excess reactant left = starting mass minus the mass that actually reacts. Use the OpenStax atomic masses from the stoichiometry lesson, plus P 30.974. Round the final answer to 4 significant figures.

worked_example.q: 10.00 g of N2 is mixed with 3.000 g of H2. N2 + 3 H2 -> 2 NH3. Which reactant is limiting?
steps: N2 would need 0.3570 times 3 = 1.071 mol of H2.
1.488 mol of H2 is more than 1.071 mol, so H2 is left over and N2 is limiting.

similar_problem.q: 20.00 g of N2 is mixed with 4.000 g of H2. N2 + 3 H2 -> 2 NH3. Which reactant is limiting?
similar_problem.hint: Turn both gram amounts into moles before you compare them with the 1-to-3 ratio.

problems.q: 10.00 g of N2 is mixed with 3.000 g of H2. N2 + 3 H2 -> 2 NH3. Which reactant is limiting? Write its formula.
problems.why: Moles of N2 = 10.00 / 28.014 = 0.3570 mol, which needs 1.071 mol of H2. Moles of H2 on hand = 3.000 / 2.016 = 1.488 mol. H2 is in excess, so N2 is limiting.
hints: 10.00 g of N2 is less than a mole. Check whether 3.000 g of H2 is more than three times that mole amount.

problems.q: 20.00 g of N2 is mixed with 4.000 g of H2. N2 + 3 H2 -> 2 NH3. Which reactant is limiting? Write its formula.
problems.why: Moles of N2 = 20.00 / 28.014 = 0.7143 mol, which needs 2.143 mol of H2. Moles of H2 on hand = 4.000 / 2.016 = 1.984 mol. H2 runs out first.
hints: 20.00 g of N2 needs three times its moles in H2. H2 is only 2.016 g/mol, so convert 4.000 g and compare.

problems.q: 20.00 g of N2 is mixed with 4.000 g of H2. N2 + 3 H2 -> 2 NH3. What is the theoretical yield of NH3 in grams?
problems.why: H2 is limiting at 4.000 / 2.016 = 1.984 mol. Moles of NH3 = 1.984 times (2/3) = 1.323 mol. Molar mass of NH3 = 14.007 + 3(1.008) = 17.031 g/mol. Mass = 1.323 times 17.031 = 22.53 g.
hints: The limiting reactant is H2. Every 3 mol H2 makes 2 mol NH3, and NH3 is 14.007 + 3(1.008) g/mol.

problems.q: The theoretical yield of NH3 from 20.00 g of N2 and 4.000 g of H2 is 22.53 g. If 18.50 g of NH3 is collected, what is the percent yield?
hints: The actual mass is 18.50 g. Divide by the theoretical ammonia mass and multiply by 100.

problems.q: 3.500 g of Al is mixed with 8.000 g of Cl2. 2 Al + 3 Cl2 -> 2 AlCl3. Which reactant is limiting? Write its formula.
problems.why: Moles of Al = 3.500 / 26.982 = 0.1297 mol, which needs 0.1946 mol of Cl2. Moles of Cl2 = 8.000 / 70.90 = 0.1128 mol. Cl2 runs out first.
hints: Convert 3.500 g of Al with 26.982 g/mol and 8.000 g of Cl2 with 70.90 g/mol, then apply the 2-to-3 ratio.

problems.q: 3.500 g of Al is mixed with 8.000 g of Cl2. 2 Al + 3 Cl2 -> 2 AlCl3. What is the theoretical yield of AlCl3 in grams?
problems.why: Cl2 is limiting at 8.000 / 70.90 = 0.1128 mol. Moles of AlCl3 = 0.1128 times (2/3) = 0.07522 mol. Molar mass of AlCl3 = 26.982 + 3(35.45) = 133.332 g/mol. Mass = 10.03 g.
hints: Cl2 limits the reaction. Two AlCl3 form from three Cl2, and AlCl3 is 26.982 + 3(35.45) g/mol.

problems.q: The theoretical yield of AlCl3 from 3.500 g of Al and 8.000 g of Cl2 is 10.03 g. If 9.000 g of AlCl3 is collected, what is the percent yield?
hints: 9.000 g was collected. Divide that actual mass by the theoretical mass of AlCl3.

problems.q: 3.500 g of Al is mixed with 8.000 g of Cl2. 2 Al + 3 Cl2 -> 2 AlCl3. How many grams of Al are left over?
problems.why: Cl2 is limiting at 0.1128 mol, so moles of Al used = 0.1128 times (2/3) = 0.07522 mol. Mass used = 0.07522 times 26.982 = 2.030 g. Left over = 3.500 - 2.030 = 1.470 g.
hints: Moles of Al that react are 2/3 of the moles of Cl2. Subtract that mass from the 3.500 g you started with.

problems.q: 0.5000 mol of P4 is mixed with 2.000 mol of O2. P4 + 5 O2 -> P4O10. Which reactant is limiting? Write its formula.
problems.why: 0.5000 mol of P4 needs 2.500 mol of O2. Only 2.000 mol of O2 is available, so O2 is limiting.
hints: 0.5000 mol of P4 would need 2.500 mol of O2, and the flask has only 2.000 mol of O2.

problems.q: 0.5000 mol of P4 is mixed with 2.000 mol of O2. P4 + 5 O2 -> P4O10. What is the theoretical yield of P4O10 in grams?
hints: The 2.000 mol of O2 produces 0.4000 mol of P4O10. Use 4(30.974) + 10(15.999) g/mol.

problems.q: The theoretical yield of P4O10 from 0.5000 mol of P4 and 2.000 mol of O2 is 113.6 g. If 96.50 g is isolated, what is the percent yield?
hints: 96.50 g was isolated. Divide by the theoretical mass of P4O10 and convert to a percent.

problems.q: 15.00 g of C2H5OH is burned with 20.00 g of O2. C2H5OH + 3 O2 -> 2 CO2 + 3 H2O. Which reactant is limiting? Write its formula.
problems.why: Molar mass of ethanol = 2(12.011) + 6(1.008) + 15.999 = 46.069 g/mol. Moles of ethanol = 15.00 / 46.069 = 0.3256 mol, which needs 0.9768 mol of O2. Moles of O2 = 20.00 / 31.998 = 0.6250 mol. O2 runs out first.
hints: Ethanol is 2(12.011) + 6(1.008) + 15.999 g/mol and needs 3 mol O2, while O2 is 31.998 g/mol.

problems.q: 15.00 g of C2H5OH is burned with 20.00 g of O2. C2H5OH + 3 O2 -> 2 CO2 + 3 H2O. What is the theoretical yield of CO2 in grams?
problems.why: O2 is limiting at 20.00 / 31.998 = 0.6250 mol. Moles of CO2 = 0.6250 times (2/3) = 0.4167 mol. Mass = 0.4167 times 44.009 = 18.34 g.
hints: O2 is limiting. Two CO2 form for every three O2, and CO2 is 44.009 g/mol.

problems.q: The theoretical yield of CO2 from 15.00 g of ethanol and 20.00 g of O2 is 18.34 g. If 14.20 g of CO2 is collected, what is the percent yield?
hints: 14.20 g of CO2 was collected. Divide by the theoretical CO2 mass from the limiting reactant.

problems.q: 15.00 g of C2H5OH is burned with 20.00 g of O2. C2H5OH + 3 O2 -> 2 CO2 + 3 H2O. How many grams of ethanol are left over?
problems.why: O2 is limiting at 0.6250 mol, so moles of ethanol used = 0.6250 / 3 = 0.2083 mol. Mass used = 0.2083 times 46.069 = 9.598 g. Left over = 15.00 - 9.598 = 5.402 g.
hints: Ethanol used, in moles, is one third of the moles of O2. Subtract that mass from 15.00 g.
